scope: shared Valkey-backed Virtual Key RPM enforcement across two separate exact-source Data Plane runtimes

environment.persistence: fresh disposable PostgreSQL 16 database and isolated least-privilege app role
environment.valkey: three local Valkey 8.1 cluster-enabled instances at 127.0.0.1:17001-17003; all nodes reached cluster_state=ok, 16384 assigned/healthy slots, 3 known nodes
environment.browser: Chromium; synthetic QA Owner; fresh first-time setup
environment.provider: none configured or called; requests intentionally used an unconfigured synthetic model

reproduction: Complete fresh instance setup through Chromium on the Control Plane.
Create an environment-bound PROVIDER Virtual Key through Access & Keys UI with allow-all model and route grants.
Use authenticated Admin API PATCH with the captured login CSRF token and If-Match version to set rpm_limit=1.
Issue one valid synthetic no-route POST /v1/chat/completions through Data Plane 18152, then a second through independent Data Plane 18153, using the one-time key in process memory only.
Inspect durable Trace rows and the key's sanitized inventory readback, then revoke the test key through the UI.

key.plaintext_evidence: not recorded; held in process memory only and discarded after requests

requests.interpretation: request admitted past key authorization/RPM limit and then failed closed because no deployment/route was configured; no upstream provider traffic
second process observed the first process's shared RPM usage and rejected before routing

visual_inspection: The key issuance form, metadata-only two-trace outcomes, key revoked inventory and three-node Operations view were visually inspected.
limits: One Virtual Key, one-minute RPM boundary, two Data Plane processes, no route/deployment.

Does not cover concurrent boundary races, TPM/budget cross-node consistency, Valkey failure/failover/rebuild, active requests, production network partitions, multiple organizations or real provider interoperability.
Three-primary test Valkey cluster had no replicas; automatic replica promotion was not tested.
